verdict.rationale: First-party docs show Unity lets developers extend the editor with custom inspectors, Editor Windows and Property Drawers, script against public Unity APIs, and add packages through the Package Manager. Editor automation is also documented through command-line arguments and the new CLI's `unity eval`, which drives the Editor directly. However, the pack never explicitly documents scripting APIs that manipulate scenes or assets: the Asset Database snippet only describes keeping source and imported assets in sync, not an editor-script API. missing for 10: explicit documentation of programmatic scene manipulation, an editor-scripting API for asset creation/modification (e.g. AssetDatabase or editor-script reference), documented plugin authoring workflow, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a game developer, I can extend and automate the editor itself — custom tools, editor scripts, plugins that manipulate scenes and assets programmatically

citations.quote: Unity lets you extend the editor with your own custom inspectors and Editor Windows and you can define how properties are displayed in the inspector with custom Property Drawers
Interacting directly with the public Unity APIs allows for finer control and a greater degree of customization.
Packages deliver a wide range of enhancements to Unity through the Package Manager.
You can launch the Unity Editor and Player with additional command line arguments to control startup behavior, configure settings, or automate workflows.
